newsitem.title: USA: Texas energy regulators seek higher state office.
newsitem.headline: Texas energy regulators seek higher state office.

text.p: Texas Railroad Commissioners Barry Williamson and Carole Keeton Rylander, two of the three top Texas energy regulators, have announced plans to square off in the state comptroller's race in 1998.
The two commissioners, both Republicans, in separate announcements on Friday said they plan to seek their party's nomination for the statewide post.

With their election bids, the commissioners joined a game of political musical chairs in Austin sparked by the surprise announcement last week that veteran Democratic Lt. Gov. Bob Bullock will not seek re-election in 1998.

Rylander, a former Austin mayor, said she will run on a platform of reducing regulation. Williamson, a former Reagan appointee to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, also stresses his fiscal conservatism and pro-market philosophy.
While on the commission, the two have clashed over Williamson's proposal to require intrastate pipelines to post their transportation prices on a commission website.
Charles Matthews, who chairs the state agency regulating Texas oil and gas production, has supported plans to develop the pricing website and quickly endorsed Williamson.
